title: AI agents now hold and spend real money, and nobody keeps their books
content:
The Desk · open beta
Your agents’ books, and a warning when one acts out of character.
Connect a wallet and the Desk opens: every agent you watch with its payments, counterparties, float and flags, measured from the public graph and dated. No password, no key, no gas to sign in.
- Liveness, spending and counterparties for each agent you watch
- Drain-shaped payments, quiet wallets and low float flagged the moment we see them
- Your watch-list stays in your browser; nothing about your agents is sent to us
Plans
Start free. Pay in USDC on Base when you need more.
Every row below is a thing the Desk or the API actually does today. Prepaid for 30 days, 90 days or a year; nothing renews by itself.
Refund of unused days within 14 days of paying, for any reason. Need the full detections feed, bulk history or a data licence? Write to us. Agents pay per call and never need an account: the x402 manifest lists every price.
How paying works
One signature, the exact amount, no gas.
- Pick a plan and a length. 30 days, 90 days or a year, priced in USDC.
- Approve the exact amount in your wallet. You sign an authorisation (EIP-3009) for that amount to our receiving address and nothing else. It cannot be reused or raised.
- Coinbase settles it on Base. Their x402 facilitator submits the transfer and pays the gas; your plan starts at once and you get the BaseScan receipt.
Where the money goes
Every payment goes straight to one published address on Base. We never hold your funds or keys, and nothing is pulled later: a plan ends when its period does.
Receiving addresssee the x402 manifest
Agents buy the same evidence packs per call over x402; the manifest at /.well-known/x402 lists every price.
Questions
What does signing in do, exactly?
You sign a plain text message that names this site, your address, a one-time code and the time (Sign-In with Ethereum). It proves you control the wallet. It creates no transaction, costs no gas and never reveals a key. A signed session stays in this browser for up to 30 days; your wallet address is your account.
Which wallets work?
Any wallet that can sign a message: MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet, Rabby, Trust, Phantom, Brave and others in the browser, or a Base Account, which signs with a passkey and needs no app or extension. On a phone, choose Base Account or open this page inside your wallet app.
How do I pay, and can I get a refund?
Plans are paid in USDC on Base from the wallet you signed in with: your wallet shows the exact amount and the receiving address before you approve, and you pay no gas. Plans are prepaid and never renew by themselves. If the Desk does not work for you, write to us within 14 days of paying and we refund the unused days; the Terms have the details.
Does the Desk work on a phone?
Yes. On a phone it opens in easy mode: the agents you watch, their flags and a switch to pause alerts, laid out for one hand. The full charts and the inspector are built for a larger screen.
Do you hold my keys or my funds?
No. The Desk only reads public records, the same API anyone can query. It never asks for a key or a recovery phrase and never signs anything for you. Nothing about the agents you watch is sent to us.

report.summary: A new open-beta dashboard tracks AI agents’ real-money payments, counterparties, and float from public blockchain data, aiming to become their missing bookkeeper.
report.background: AI agents increasingly get wallets and can autonomously pay APIs, services, and each other, often via stablecoins and machine-payment protocols like x402. This enables agent commerce but creates an accounting gap: who tracks what an agent spent, earned, owes, or holds? Traditional finance tools assume humans, bank accounts, and identity. On-chain payments are public but fragmented across addresses, chains, and facilitators. The Desk, from Agentic Finance Graph, enters open beta as an observability layer: connect a wallet, watch agents, and see payments, counterparties, float, and anomaly flags derived from public graph data. It reflects growing demand for auditability, risk controls, and bookkeeping as autonomous agents move from demos to real money.
key_points: Connect a wallet and the Desk opens a dashboard for every agent you watch, showing liveness, spending, counterparties, float and dated flags measured from public blockchain data. Sign-in uses SIWE: a plain text signature, no password, no key, no gas, and no transaction.

The Desk flags drain-shaped payments, quiet wallets and low float as soon as it sees them. These heuristics target common failure modes: an agent being exploited, going dormant, or running out of operating funds. Alerts can be paused on mobile.

Privacy is local-first: your watch-list stays in your browser, and nothing about the agents you watch is sent to the service. The product only reads public records, the same API anyone can query, and never asks for keys or recovery phrases.

Pricing is prepaid in USDC on Base. Users approve an exact amount with one EIP-3009 signature; Coinbase's x402 facilitator settles and pays gas. Agents can buy evidence packs per call via x402, with prices in the x402 manifest, and unused days are refundable within 14 days.

The Desk works on desktop and phone, with a simplified mobile mode for watching agents, flags and alert pausing; full charts and inspector need a larger screen. BaseScan receipts provide payment proof, and the service says it never holds funds or keys.
report.impact: The Desk points to a missing layer in the agent economy: financial accountability. As AI agents gain wallets and spend stablecoins, businesses need audit trails, anomaly detection, and float management before they can trust agents with real budgets. For developers, it suggests a pattern: expose agent activity as queryable public data, sell monitoring via x402, and let agents pay per call. For regular users, it could make autonomous payments more transparent and safer, but only if dashboards are accurate and public-chain data is enough. It also highlights risks: on-chain transparency may not map cleanly to off-chain intent, and watch-lists remain local, so shared compliance still needs work.
report.tools: Follow the Agentic Finance Graph Desk (agenticfinancegraph.com/desk), its x402 manifest, and BaseScan for receipts. Relevant rails and standards include Coinbase’s x402 facilitator, Base, USDC, EIP-3009 transfer authorizations, and Sign-In with Ethereum. Compatible wallets include MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet, Rabby, Trust, Phantom, Brave, and Base Account. For similar monitoring, watch blockchain indexers, stablecoin payment APIs, and emerging agent-accounting/audit projects.
